Advancement of Junior Scholars
The Center for Junior Scholars (CJS) is the central institution to support doctoral researchers, postdocs and research group leaders.
We offer the best possible support throughout your career, from planning your doctorate to your postdoctoral qualification, and are happy to advise you on any questions you may have.
The CJS provides you with access to the extensive range of counseling services and academic continuing education programs at TU Berlin. We bundle information on funding opportunities, offer specific programs for the advancement of women in science with proMotion and ProFiL, and strive for the strategic development of the advancement of junior scholars in higher education policy.
Click here for a quick introduction to everything the Center for Junior Scholars has to offer!
Go to the INFO PORTAL
Your direct contact to us
If you have any questions you would like to discuss, please visit our weekly online consultation (Mondays 11:00 - 12:00) or feel free to contact us directly.
We are always available by phone and e-mail.

© Philipp Arnoldt
Advising & Support
The Center for Junior Scholars is available to answer all your questions, whether you are considering doing a doctorate at Technische Universität Berlin, already completing a doctorate at the University, or are here as a postdoc. Expert advising and support are offered on a wide range of issues relating to the advancement of junior scholars.
more
© Maura Barbulescu
Doctorate
Pursuing a doctorate is an interesting option for many graduates and not only those looking to develop a career in academia. There are many reasons for doing a doctorate. Students obtaining a sufficiently good average grade in their first degree programs are in a particularly good position to pursue this option. They will also need to find a doctoral supervisor. Dissertations can be completed either as an individual supervised project or as part of a structured doctoral program.
more
© science photo
Postdoc Phase
The postdoc phase represents the next stage in an academic career after completing a doctorate. Technische Universität Berlin offers junior scholars a wide range of excellent support and funding options geared to the specific challenges faced at the outset of a career in research.
more
© Iakov Filimonov
Continuing Education & Further Qualification

© smolaw
International
In an increasingly globalized academic world, international exchange is becoming standard practice in all areas and forms an important and beneficial aspect of an academic career. Technische Universität Berlin places particular attention on strengthening the international focus of its junior scholars.
more
proMotion program
proMotion – Qualification, exchange and networking for female PhD students
proMotion training is a workshop program for a fixed group of female PhD students. proMotion support offers lunch talks and information sessions on PhD research and career planning. In addition, counselling and coaching are available for female PhD researchers.
more
ProFiL Programme
The ProFiL Programme offers career support for female researchers with a PhD who are on the path to a professorship, through a specialised workshop programme, networking opportunities and intensive mentoring.
more
© Tim Gouw
Gender Equality
Technische Universität Berlin is actively committed to achieving equal opportunities and work-family life balance. The advancement of female junior scholars has been a key priority for a number of years. Through its Diversity Strategy, the University is intensifying its efforts by increasing its focus on other aspects of gender equality.
more

If you have ever wondered which competencies you acquire during an academic career in addition to your professional expertise, then the competence model and the associated online competence tool may be of interest to you!

Career tracking study (Verbleibsstudie)
The career tracking study of women (and men) with doctorates is intended to provide information about the various career paths of TUB graduates.

Good Supervision Culture A project within the framework of the Berlin University Alliance
The “Good Supervision Culture” project aims to advance discussion about supervision processes - with the overarching goal of harmonizing and improving conditions for doctoral researchers at all BUA institutions.
